summary: H.J. Res. 142 is a joint resolution that disapproves and nullifies a District of Columbia law that had decoupled local D.C. taxes from federal tax law changes enacted in 2025. By overturning the D.C. legislation, this resolution puts D.C. tax law back in conformity with the federal 2025 reconciliation act.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to D.C. tax laws that match the 2025 federal reconciliation act, affecting standard deductions, age-based deductions, and deductions for tips, overtime, and car loan interest.
Subject to federal-aligned depreciation allowances and 100% deductions for research and experimental costs retroactive to tax year 2022.

key_provisions: Nullifies the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025.
Reinstates a higher basic standard deduction for D.C. taxpayers.
Increases deductible charitable cash contributions for taxpayers taking the standard deduction.
Establishes a $6,000 tax deduction for taxpayers aged 65 and older.
Allows tax deductions for qualified tips, qualified overtime pay, and qualified car loan interest.
Authorizes an elective 100% depreciation allowance for nonresidential real property and allows businesses to deduct 100% of research and experimental costs retroactive to tax year 2022.
Negates other D.C. changes, including the restoration of the D.C. child tax credit.

summary_detail.significance: The joint resolution directly overrides local D.C. legislation regarding taxation, aligning D.C. tax rules with federal tax provisions and reversing local efforts to decouple from federal tax law changes.
